ranking.name: Rain and snow (precipitation)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, rain and snow (precipitation) in Southeast Asia changed by +0.36 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval +0.08 to +0.63), which is statistically significant (p = 0.01). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.89 mm/day.

cautions: Only 24% of this region's area has land cells with data in at least 95% of the months, so the result describes only that part.

ranking.name: Water in the topsoil
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water in the topsoil in Southeast Asia shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.44): the estimate is −0.13 kg/m² per decade (95% confidence interval −0.47 to +0.20). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.
